question: China has recently turned its rare earth exports into a bargaining chip, exposing the EU’s heavy dependence on permanent magnets used in the wind and automotive industries, as well as in much electronic and medical equipment.

Although the Critical Raw Materials Act sets a target of 25 % of critical materials from recycled sources by 2030 and the RESourceEU Action Plan, adopted on 3 December 2025, aims to move this along, there is still no structured EU chain for collecting, disassembling and recycling these magnets.

Some EU recyclers of rare earths from end-of-life products point to elevated costs compared to Asian manufacturers, insufficient market signals and overly slow procedures for authorising new capacity. 1.

In light of the above, does the Commission plan to put forward, under the RESourceEU plan, a specific regulatory framework aiming to establish a permanent magnet recycling sector within the EU, including requirements for the magnets to be designed to be easily disassembled?

Does it intend to bring in financial incentives and/or quotas for incorporating recycled materials to support construction of rare-earth recycling and refining facilities and make value chains more resilient?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.2.2026) The Commission shares the assessment of the strategic importance of rare earth elements and permanent magnets for the EU’s green and digital transitions and the need to reduce excessive external dependencies.

Under the RESourceEU Action Plan1 and the targeted amendment to the European Critical Raw Materials Act2 (CRMA), the Commission adopted measures to accelerate the deployment of recycling technologies for strategic materials.

In particular, the amendments to the CRMA propose to extend the list of products required to bear information on the presence of permanent magnets, with a view to easing their identification, dismantling and recovery.

It is also proposed to include pre-consumer waste alongside post-consumer waste, thereby supporting increased recycling of permanent magnets in the EU and facilitating the uptake of secondary permanent magnets in products. As per the CRMA, the Commission is already working on the possibility of setting quotas of recycled content for permanent magnets.

Including pre consumer waste as feedstock for recycling would contribute to boosting the EU recycling capacity. The RESourceEU Action Plan also puts strong emphasis on financing by setting up a CRM financing hub that will mobilise EUR 3 billion in support of projects all along the CRM value chain.
